summary: Tenant event context lost when SIEM JSONL wrapper combines multi-event batches
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that when Redwood packages audit events into our JSONL SIEM export wrapper (daily and ad-hoc slices), tenant-scoped context (tenant_id, session_id, request_context.*) is occasionally missing or collapsed into a generic envelope. Impact: NordicsBank cannot reconcile per-tenant activity in their SIEM, failing a regulatory playback test for transaction traceability (affects compliance proof). Observed behavior: - Batches with >200 events occasionally show a single top-level 'tenant_context' object rather than per-event context. - Missing session_id on downstream Splunk/Hec ingestion. Expected behavior: Each event line in JSONL should contain full per-event metadata (tenant_id, request_id, session_id, user_agent, region) and the wrapper must not deduplicate or hoist tenant fields across lines. Environment: prod export pipeline (s3 batch exporter), customer configured signed S3 delivery + Splunk HEC consuming via a Redpiper connector. Time window: problem observed intermittently between 2026-03-07 and 2026-03-09 during a high-volume replay test.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer requests on-demand JSONL export for tenant T-98234 covering 2026-03-07 00:00 to 2026-03-07 06:00.
2) Redwood export job packages events into line-delimited JSON (wrapper version v2.3.0).
3) Job writes compressed .jsonl.gz to customer's S3 bucket; Splunk connector pulls and ingests.
4) Customer runs their reconciliation that expects per-line tenant/session keys.
5) They observe intermittent lines where tenant fields are either absent or a single envelope object appears at top of file.
Repro notes: Issue rate increased with bursts where >200 events per batch were generated; smaller batches do not show the problem consistently.
investigation_notes: Initial hypotheses: (A) JSONL wrapper v2.3.0 attempted an optimization to deduplicate identical tenant_context across consecutive events and mistakenly hoisted the object as a separate line; (B) Streaming serializer had a buffer flush boundary that emitted context object when a size threshold was reached; (C) Post-processing compressor/concat stage introduced line breaks that separated context from events. Actions taken: - Pulled export artifacts from the customer's S3 bucket for the time windows; reproduced the envelope pattern locally. - Cross-checked wrapper code in repo; found recent change in platform PR #939 that added a cross-batch 'context pool' to reduce payload size. - Triggered a local export using the same dataset and wrapper v2.3.0; observed same envelope when batch size >128KB. - Rolled test with wrapper v2.2.7 (previous stable) and did not reproduce. Observed correlation with batch size and with events where per-event metadata fields compressed to identical JSON, triggering dedup step. Telemetry/dashboards referenced: export-job-traces (trace ids: trace-7f3a, trace-7f8b), serializer-flush-metrics. Hypothesis now leans to (A) dedupe/hoist optimization bug in v2.3.0. Next steps: revert dedupe logic or gate behind stable flag for enterprise customers; create regression test for JSONL invariants.

resolution: Workaround: For immediate compliance playback, Support created an on-demand export using wrapper v2.2.7 which preserved per-event context. We delivered that export to the customer's secure S3 staging and confirmed their reconciliation passed. Permanent fix plan: revert/patch dedupe/hoist optimization in wrapper v2.3.0 and release v2.3.1 with a regression test covering JSONL per-line invariants.
